Thanks for the demo last week. Legal asked us to confirm a couple of commercial items before we can sign:

- We need clarity on the invoicing cadence for the annual commit and whether Redwood can issue a single upfront invoice or must split into tranches for our accounting.

- Net terms: your order form references Net 45 but our procurement requires Net 30 — what's possible?

Attached is the order form with minimal redlines from Acme legal (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Can you review and confirm the expected path to sign?

Susan —

Thanks for the redlines and for flagging the tax point. Quick answers up front:

1) Invoicing cadence: we can support either a single upfront invoice or a three-tranche schedule tied to activation dates. Either approach is fine operationally — the difference is how accounting records revenue and how your AP processes large upfront POs.

2) Withholding tax: Redwood typically gross-ups for customer withholding only when there is an explicit tax clause in the order form and when we receive official withholding documentation post-payment. We can discuss a withholding language option where Acme withholds and we provide a tax residency / article 12 certificate afterward. Karthik, Marissa — please confirm legal and tax ops requirements.

3) Net terms: our standard is Net 45 for customers on enterprise terms, but we can do Net 30 for a small fee (0.5% discount reduction) or trade for an earlier invoice trigger (e.g., invoiced on signature instead of activation).

I'll loop in our legal/tax owners and propose redline language for the withholding flow by EOD.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa —

Forwarding Acme's note. My quick take (tax/legal):

- For EU withholding: we need Acme to confirm the tax regime (country & section). If Acme is applying withholding, we typically accept (a) the customer withholds, (b) we request a signed certificate of withholding and local tax receipt within 60 days, and (c) Redwood will provide a gross-up invoice adjustment or a credit once proof is received.
- Language suggestion: add a clause to the order form: "If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold taxes, Customer shall withhold and pay such taxes to the appropriate authorities and provide Redwood with official documentation within sixty (60) days; Redwood will issue a credit or gross-up adjustment upon receipt of such documentation."
- On Net terms: operationally okay to move to Net 30 for strategic deals; we should capture an administrative fee or trade for a shorter invoice schedule.

I'll draft the redline. Marissa — can you own the revenue recognition and billing ops impacts?

Karthik
